meta.synthetic_note: KYC risk class, review dates, risk profile and vulnerability are synthetic, generated for this prototype independently of the real data.

agent_steps.name: Get segment
reads: products added and closed in the last three and six months
agent_steps.returns: The client's group with a plain description, the profile shown to the advisor, and change flags.
agent_steps.rule_or_model: k means with k = 6 on standardised profile and holding features, chosen by silhouette. Change flags are fixed rules, for example: at least one product added in the last three months.

agent_steps.name: Get propensities
reads: history up to the month before the meeting only
sex and place of birth are never read
agent_steps.returns: A take up score for every modelled product the client does not hold yet, with the observed take up rate of that score band in the test month and what the score leans on.
agent_steps.rule_or_model: One LightGBM model per product, trained on clients who did not hold it yet. SHAP contributions turned into short phrases for the reasons.

agent_steps.name: Check suitability
reads: salary, pension and payroll already arriving
agent_steps.returns: Products held back with the rule that fired and its reason, products that are likely already in progress, and whether the brief should open with a care check.
agent_steps.rule_or_model: Ten transparent guardrail rules, checked for every product scoring 10% or more, plus one linked income rule. A high score never overrides a rule. The care check opens the brief when the client is marked possibly vulnerable or their activity dropped.

agent_steps.name: Check review due
reads: last and next periodic review date (synthetic)
agent_steps.returns: Whether the periodic review is overdue, due within the window or not due, and the days until it.
agent_steps.rule_or_model: Due when the next review falls within 90 days of the meeting. Illustrative intervals: 5 years for low risk, 3 for medium, 1 for high.

agent_steps.name: Draft questions
reads: the top suggestion and its score band
agent_steps.returns: Two or three questions, each with the reason it is asked and two or three likely answers that show how the brief would change.
agent_steps.rule_or_model: Fixed templates in priority order (due review, recent changes, top suggestion, open) and fixed answer rules in branches.py. Claude may only rephrase the wording, when a key is set.

novelty.point: Says what not to offer, and why.

# Meeting brief: Client 01

Meeting on 1 June 2016. Prepared to support the conversation. Scores are estimates, not instructions; the advisor decides what to discuss.

## 1. Who this client is

**Younger students** (cluster 0): Mostly students (99%), younger (average age 24), newer clients (about 3 years with the bank).

Aged 25, with the bank for 3 years, recorded income about 38,000, student segment, holds 1 product: Payroll account.

Recent changes:
- No notable changes in the last six months.

## 2. What might help

- **Current account**, scores above 50%. In the test month, 45% of the 377 clients scoring between 50% and 100% took it up. The score leans on: already holds a payroll account; aged 25; holds 1 product.

## 3. What not to offer

No high scoring product was held back by the suitability check.

## 4. Due anyway

No periodic review is due within 90 days; the next one is on 18 October 2019.

*Review dates come from a synthetic layer made for this prototype, not real records.*

## 5. Questions to open with

1. How do you handle your everyday payments at the moment?
   *Top suggestion. Why: In the test month, 45% of the 377 clients scoring between 50% and 100% took up current account.*
   - If "Open to talking about it": Discuss Current account if the client wants to.
   - If "Already arranged elsewhere": Nothing new is raised. Current account is arranged at another bank. Record where it is arranged and do not raise Current account again in this meeting. Record it as declined: the brief will not raise Current account again for 182 days.
   - If "Not a priority now": Nothing new is raised. Current account is not a priority for the client now. Record it as declined: the brief will not raise Current account again for 182 days.
2. What matters most to you financially over the next year?
   *Open. Why: No due review, recent change or suggestion to start from, so an open question.*
   - If "Raises something specific": Record what the client raises; the brief has no data on it.
   - If "Nothing in particular": No change to the brief.

## How this brief was prepared

1. `get_profile`: aged 25, 1 product held
2. `get_segment`: cluster 0, Younger students
3. `get_recent_changes`: no change flags
4. `get_propensities`: 7 products scored, highest Current account (above 50%)
5. `check_suitability`: Current account: allowed
6. `check_care`: care check: no signs in the data
7. `check_review_due`: not due, next review 2019-10-18 (1234 days)
8. `draft_questions`: 2 questions drafted, each with a reason and answer branches

# Meeting brief: Client 39

Meeting on 1 June 2016. Prepared to support the conversation. Scores are estimates, not instructions; the advisor decides what to discuss.

## 1. Who this client is

**Active everyday clients** (cluster 1): Mostly active (99% active), everyday individual segment (99%), often hold a current account (92%).

Aged 27, with the bank for 2 months, income not recorded, individual segment, holds 1 product: Current account.

Recent changes:
- Took up 1 new product in the last three months.
- Joined 2 months ago.

## 2. What might help

- **Bills paid by direct debit**, scores 10%. In the test month, 14% of the 2,684 clients scoring between 10% and 20% took it up. The score leans on: an active client; aged 27; added 1 product in the last six months.

## 3. What not to offer

fairness.note: Groups are used only to audit the output. Sex is not a model feature. Rates are measured on the briefed clients; ranking quality on the test month, where labels exist.

limits.title: Linked products and leakage
limits.text: Salary paid in, pension paid in and the payroll account tend to arrive together (salary and pension start in the same month for almost every client, so the brief shows them as one signal), so part of what those models learn is that one follows the other. The brief marks them as likely already in progress instead of suggesting them, and keeps them in the metrics. Features only use history up to the month before the target month, so the label never leaks into them.

limits.title: The KYC layer is synthetic
limits.text: Review dates, risk class, risk profile and vulnerability are made up with a fixed seed, independently of the real data. The rules and review intervals are illustrative.

limits.title: Spanish retail data, 2015-01 to 2016-05
limits.text: The patterns come from one Spanish bank's anonymised clients in that period. They may not hold for other markets, products or years, and the score says nothing about intent.

limits.title: The plus account sample is small
limits.text: Only 113 take ups in the test month. The lift over the baseline has a 95% interval from -0.014 to +0.039, so it is not clearly better than logistic regression for this product.

limits.title: One test month
limits.text: Every metric comes from 2016-05 alone; another month could look different.

limits.title: No learning from advisors yet
limits.text: When an advisor records a decline, the brief does not raise that product again for 182 days. There are no real advisors here, so the log is empty and nothing is learned from it. With real logs, declines could become a feature or a negative label for the models; I do not fake that with made up records.

limits.title: Care signals are limited
limits.text: The care check reads only the synthetic vulnerability flag and a drop in activity. The data has no debts, arrears or spending, so it cannot spot over borrowing; an advisor still has to ask.
